messages:
incident-bot: Pager: EGRESS PATH INSTABILITY detected for west-us5 at 2026-03-15T07:12:47Z (2361234567). Symptoms: outbound TCP failures, late SYN retries, elevated 502/504s for flows egressing via nat-west-us5-01. Severity: P2.
oncall-sf: ack. I'm taking lead for on-call. @mira please grab packet captures and conntrack stats. @ash please check peering and BGP state.
mira (sre): grabbing tcpdump and nf_conntrack dump from nat-west-us5-01. preliminary: conntrack growth starting ~07:10 UTC, lots of TIME_WAIT & orphaned entries. seeing large number of retransmits from same prefixes.
ash (netops): I'm seeing intermittent BGP withdraws on the transit peer to west-us5-pop from EdgeWave. NOC ticket opened (EW-8421). Pulling RIBs now.
jesse (prod-eng): App layer shows spike in 5xxs for some Dedicated pools and a handful of Private egress routes that explicitly NAT through nat-west-us5-01. Recording impacted pool IDs: dpool-wus5-1, dpool-wus5-2.
kelly (support): Support is getting calls. Preparing customer-contact list for those dedicated pools and any customers with pinned egress. Need a short blurb for targeted emails.
oncall-sf: Mitigation plan proposal: 1) shift affected prefix routing to nat-west-us3 as a temporary egress; 2) apply safe conntrack threshold increase on nat-west-us5-01; 3) coordinate with EdgeWave for stable peering. Who can perform step 1? @ash
ash (netops): I can execute an async route preference change. Using runbook script to nudge traffic to nat-west-us3 with a gradual weight. Will post command and run now.
ash (netops): running:
```
# runbook: nudge egress to west-us3
curl -s -X POST "https://orchestrator.internal/run/route-adjust" -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' -d '{"prefix":"10.64.0.0/14","from":"nat-west-us5-01","to":"nat-west-us3-01","strategy":"weighted","weight":75}'
```
mira (sre): starting conntrack bump as temporary stop-gap on nat-west-us5-01, per runbook safe limits:
```
echo 200000 > /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=86400
```
mira (sre): applied changes and monitoring. Also exported tcpdump slices to /tmp/egress_wus5_07_12.pcap for postmortem.
incident-bot: Dashboards: https://dash.redwood-infra/internal/incidents/2361234567 (auth required). Alert graph: outbound reset rate, conntrack count, provider BGP updates.
ash (netops): route adjustment completed at 07:15:10 UTC. BGP convergence observed, traffic shifting to nat-west-us3. Watching for errors to drop.
jesse (prod-eng): quick customer-facing status suggestion: "We are aware of an issue impacting outbound network connectivity from west-us5 that may cause failed requests or increased latency for some customers. Traffic has been rerouted to an alternate path and engineers are monitoring. We will provide updates every 30 minutes or on important changes."
commops-bot: Draft targeted email for Dedicated customers (short): Subject: "Incident: Outbound networking interruptions in west-us5 — mitigation in progress" Body: "Hi — We detected networking issues affecting outbound connections for some Dedicated pools in west-us5 starting ~07:10 UTC. We've initiated traffic reroutes to an alternate NAT and are monitoring. If you have a private egress path pinned to nat-west-us5-01, our team may reach out with next steps. — Redwood Inference Ops"
kelly (support): sending targeted messages to owners of dpool-wus5-1 and dpool-wus5-2 and to contact for customer-88 (private cluster) at 07:18 UTC.
mira (sre): telemetry: conntrack count dropped after route shift, reset rate down ~85%. 5xxs trending down but a few residual errors from stickiness/pinned flows.
ash (netops): EdgeWave NOC update: intermittent route flap observed on their ATT link, mitigation in progress on their side. They plan full stabilization in the next 20–40 minutes. Ticket EW-8421 updated at 07:20 UTC.
oncall-sf: Internal comms snippet for #eng and #product:
```
Heads-up: transient egress failures observed for west-us5 due to transit peer instability. We shifted traffic to nat-west-us3; monitoring. On-call: @oncall-sf, SRE: @mira, NetOps: @ash, Support: @kelly. No code rollback needed.
```
commops-bot: Status page update queued (public): "07:20 UTC — We are investigating outbound networking instability in west-us5. Mitigation: traffic rerouted to alternate NAT. Some requests may still fail or be delayed. Next update in 30 minutes or on material change."
oncall-sf: Action items: - Keep status page updated every 30m - Support to maintain customer-targeted outreach until error rates normalize - NetOps hold reroute until provider confirms fix (or 1h) - SRE collect artifacts and start incident write-up. Any additions?
jesse (prod-eng): please add an SLA-impact note if >30m of sustained errors for affected tenants.
kelly (support): confirming emails sent to all affected owners at 07:21 UTC. saved copies to /ops/customer-comms/2361234567/
mira (sre): will keep packet captures and conntrack dumps archived. tagging for postmortem: suspect provider-induced route churn causing conntrack growth and subsequent TCP resets on our NAT box.
alerts-bot: Automated healthcheck: outbound resets normalized at 07:28:33 UTC. Rate < baseline threshold.
mira (sre): provider now reporting stabilized peering at 07:32 UTC per NOC message. We'll keep reroute in place for an hour to ensure no recurrence.
oncall-sf: thanks all. I'll start post-incident template and schedule RCA. Reopening thread if we see regressions. Last update timestamp appended.
incident-bot: Incident thread auto-archived. last_update: 2361236000.
